items.evidence: The notes describe the sixth-floor location and room layout, but do not state that the project manager opened the meeting and presented that overview.
The notes cover occupancy limits and say the lounge's purpose remains open, but do not clearly capture the question of whether a lounge was necessary or the project manager's response.

Furniture and shared-equipment constraints are covered. The discussion about possibly not getting the space is missing. The transcript clarifies that the rooms were promised; the more substantive concern was accommodating additional people.
"The group is tasked with developing a room assignment plan that balances preferences, project teams, and space constraints."
The notes cover professor/assistant sharing, project grouping, phone noise, physical room splitting, meeting spaces, visitors, smoking, Gisella, and administrative-office allocation.
The amenities section covers the absence of a dedicated cafeteria and coffee machines on the first and third floors.
Andrei is assigned to "Investigate the possibility and administrative feasibility of physically splitting rooms"; the notes also identify walls and doors as the relevant modifications.
Andrei is assigned to ask about administrative location options outside the new space, "including possibility of sharing with related admin staff."
The notes call for collecting proposals and "names and preferences from all members."
"All participants" are assigned to "Poll colleagues and assistants for their personal preferences."
The notes describe collecting concrete seating proposals with names and preferences and developing a plan that balances individual needs.
"Multiple proposals will be merged and negotiated with the other group's suggestions."
The action list assigns following up with Maggie and Pierrette to Andrei. Susan explicitly volunteers to ask them at 30:54.
"Schedule next meeting for Tuesday afternoon (around 14:00)." The transcript likewise agrees to next Tuesday at about two o'clock.

"Grouping by project is less practical" captures the reasoning, but the notes describe it as a lower priority rather than clearly stating that project grouping was rejected as the organizing principle.

"Options include giving admin a one-person room or a two-person room, but the second desk's use remains unclear." This matches the transcript: no final assignment was made. The answer key overstates a proposal as a decision; senior visitors sharing with Gisella were rejected.
"No dedicated cafeteria." This accurately refers to the group's own space, not the building, which already has a downstairs cafeteria.
The notes discuss furniture limiting occupancy and investigating "four desks in a three-person room."
"Preference gathering emphasized as critical for success to avoid unnecessary rework and respect individual needs."
The notes discuss sharing with assistants and separately evaluate grouping people by project.
"Splitting rooms to create private offices was discussed" and investigating physical splits or partitions is listed.
The notes emphasize a need for the lounge and uncertainty about its functions, but omit Susan's explicit question, "Do we really need that?"
The notes cover limited visitor capacity, denser room layouts, lounge overflow, and appropriate accommodation for senior visitors.
"Gisela's role involves high communication and noise, making shared office space difficult."
The notes discuss allocating a one-person or two-person administrative office and exploring placement with other school administrators.
The amenities section addresses the cafeteria question and distinguishes the group's space from the building's existing cafeteria.
"There are two vending machines on the first and third floors for coffee."

errors.claim: There are "18 desks for 15 people including a reading room" and "18 desks for 15 people, including reading room and visitor spaces."
errors.why_wrong: Eighteen is the nominal capacity of all the rooms before allocating a lounge. The transcript explicitly calculates that using a two-person room as the reading room leaves sixteen work positions for fifteen people, not eighteen usable desks with the lounge already provided.

errors.claim: "Merge proposals with another group before next Tuesday's review meeting."
errors.why_wrong: No such deadline was agreed. The next meeting was intended to develop a coherent proposal, which would then be merged with the other group's proposal when available.

errors.claim: "Part-time schedules reduce desk demand, offering some flexibility."
errors.why_wrong: The group explicitly agreed that every person, including part-time staff, needs a separate desk. Part-time attendance reduces simultaneous occupancy and congestion, not the number of desks required.

errors.claim: "Growth is effectively zero unless visitors or temporary staff share existing desks."
errors.why_wrong: Sharing existing desks was not the agreed solution. The discussion considered adding a fourth separate place to larger rooms and using the lounge for overflow, while explicitly rejecting two people using the same desk.

errors.claim: "Desk sizes and filing cabinet needs limit sharing desks between part-time personnel."
errors.why_wrong: Desk size was discussed as a constraint on fitting additional desks into rooms, not on sharing a desk. Desk sharing was rejected because each person wanted their own desk and personal storage.

errors.claim: Under Andrei: "Follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette) to gather their office arrangement preferences before next meeting."
errors.why_wrong: Susan, not Andre, explicitly undertook to ask Maggie and Pierrette about their preferences.

errors.claim: "New office space details and constraints clarified ... (00:06)."
errors.why_wrong: The transcript contains no office-layout discussion at 00:06. The substantive opening begins at 00:54, followed by the layout overview.
